bull.t: Recurring Revenue and Installed Base Expansion
bull.b: Growth in recurring revenue and the validated installed base supports a more durable business model than relying only on one-time instrument sales. As customers use more systems, consumables and service revenue can compound, improving revenue visibility and customer retention over time.

Consumables growth above 20% indicates increasing routine utilization of the Growth Direct platform and strengthens the recurring-revenue engine. Higher usage per installed system can deepen customer integration, support future revenue expansion, and improve the economics of placements.

The improvement in gross and service margins demonstrates operational progress and provides evidence that the model can become more profitable as scale and service productivity improve. Management’s targets for higher margins through 2026 reinforce the potential for lasting earnings improvement.

bear.b: Large recurring operating losses remain a fundamental constraint despite improving revenue and gross margins. Continued losses reduce internal funding capacity, require management to prioritize cost reduction and scale, and leave the company without demonstrated operating leverage or near-term breakeven.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow means growth is not yet self-funded and keeps liquidity dependent on external capital. Reliance on debt milestones or warrant proceeds can restrict strategic flexibility and exposes the business to execution risk if planned funding is delayed.

Higher leverage combined with declining equity and assets reduces the company’s financial flexibility while losses continue. A more leveraged balance sheet can increase financing pressure, limit investment choices, and make it harder to absorb delays in placements, validation, or margin improvement.
